title: Question 13
stem:
Beryllium-7 ($^{7}_{4}\text{Be}$) is produced in the upper atmosphere and then sinks down onto the Earth's surface. Nuclei of beryllium-7 decay with a half-life of $53.3 \text{ days}$ to form stable nuclei.

The activity of a sample of beryllium-7 on a tree leaf is $39 \text{ mBq}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Show that the decay constant of beryllium-7 is $1.5 \times 10^{-7} \text{ s}^{-1}$.
hints: Hint 1: Think about how half-life and decay constant are linked, and remember the decay constant must end up in per second, so the half-life must first be in seconds.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Link half-life to decay constant**
You know that a larger decay constant means faster decay and shorter half-life. They are inversely related by $\lambda = \ln 2 / T_{1/2}$ where $T_{1/2}$ must be in seconds to give $\lambda$ in $\text{s}^{-1}$.

Step 2: **Convert days to seconds and calculate**
First change 53.3 days into seconds: $$T_{1/2} = 53.3 \times 24 \times 60 \times 60 = 4.605 \times 10^{6} \text{ s}$$ Then: $$\lambda = \frac{0.693}{4.605 \times 10^{6}} = 1.50 \times 10^{-7} \text{ s}^{-1}$$ This shows the required value.

key_concepts: unit conversion from days to seconds

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Determine the mass of the beryllium-7 on the leaf.
hints: Hint 1: Activity tells you how many decays per second are happening. Think about how that rate depends on how many unstable nuclei you have and how likely each one is to decay.
Hint 2: Convert the 39 mBq activity into Bq (decays per second) and use your value of decay constant to work out how many beryllium-7 nuclei $N$ must be present.
Hint 3: Each beryllium-7 nucleus has nucleon number 7, so its mass is about 7 times the mass of one nucleon. Think how to go from the number of nuclei to total mass in kg.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Find the number of nuclei from activity**
Activity is the decay rate, $A = \lambda N$. So the number of undecayed nuclei is $N = A / \lambda$. Convert activity to SI: $$A = 39 \text{ mBq} = 39 \times 10^{-3} \text{ Bq} = 0.039 \text{ s}^{-1}$$ Then: $$N = \frac{0.039}{1.5 \times 10^{-7}} = 2.6 \times 10^{5}$$ Only about a quarter of a million atoms are present, which is why the mass will be tiny.

Step 2: **Find the mass of one beryllium-7 nucleus**
Beryllium-7 has nucleon number 7, so one nucleus has mass approximately $7u$, where $u = 1.66 \times 10^{-27} \text{ kg}$. $$m_{1} = 7 \times 1.66 \times 10^{-27} = 1.16 \times 10^{-26} \text{ kg}$$

Step 3: **Calculate total mass**
Multiply number by mass per nucleus: $$m = N m_{1} = 2.6 \times 10^{5} \times 1.16 \times 10^{-26} = 3.0 \times 10^{-21} \text{ kg}$$

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The leaf is covered so that no further beryllium-7 is added to the existing sample from the atmosphere.

Calculate the time that must elapse before the activity of the sample is reduced to $2.0 \text{ mBq}$.
hints: Hint 1: No new nuclei are added, so the activity falls exponentially with time. Think about which starting and final activities you need to compare.
Hint 2: Set up the exponential relation between the two activities and the time, then take natural logs to solve for $t$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Write the activity decay equation**
Because activity is proportional to $N$, it follows the same exponential law: $$A = A_{0} e^{-\lambda t}$$ Here $A_{0} = 39 \text{ mBq}$ and $A = 2.0 \text{ mBq}$. So: $$\frac{2.0}{39} = e^{-\lambda t}$$

Step 2: **Solve for time by taking logs**
Take natural log of both sides: $$\ln\left(\frac{2.0}{39}\right) = -\lambda t$$ $$t = \frac{-\ln(2.0/39)}{1.5 \times 10^{-7}} = \frac{2.97}{1.5 \times 10^{-7}} = 2.0 \times 10^{7} \text{ s}$$ This is about 230 days, over 4 half-lives, which makes sense for a fall by a factor of about 20.
